interpretation.dragTiming: Each ~5s the driver sends one pointermove. Total drag 1step = 32s. The TapNow React Flow processes all moves correctly without drops.
interpretation.lossAnalysis: First drag: 50→42 (8px). Second drag: 180→156 (24px). Each request loses 8-24px. Pattern suggests **edge clamping or initial-position offset**, NOT grid snap (which would snap to multiples). The first pixel after pointerdown is consumed by 'selecting' before drag starts.
interpretation.edgeBehavior: No snap, no bounce, no wall. Text node can be dragged past sidebar (overlaps) and presumably off-screen. **No bounds enforcement in TapNow** = true infinite canvas.
interpretation.noSnapLine: No `.react-flow__snapline` or snap class found. Snap-to-grid toggle exists in toolbar (V2 §10.4) but defaults to OFF. V3 confirms: no implicit snap.
interpretation.css_evidence: Node position is stored as CSS transform translate(x, y), not React state. The drag is React Flow's internal pointermove handler that updates transform style directly.
